paper.title: Parameterizing Vertical Mixing Coefficients in the Ocean Surface Boundary Layer using Neural Networks
paper.venue: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems (submitted; arXiv:2306.09045v3)

methods.canonical_name: ePBL NN (neural-network eddy diffusivity shape function and velocity scale inside ePBL)
methods.family_raw: neural networks N1 and N2 implemented within the physics-based ePBL scheme
methods.architecture_note: Two feed-forward MLPs (ReLU), 2 hidden layers x 32 nodes each: N1 (4 inputs f,B0,u*,h -> 16 outputs g(sigma)) and N2 (3 inputs -> scalar v0). Classified HYBRID_PHYSICS_ML by arbitration rule 1 (learned network embedded in a physical scheme); MLP_DNN is the architecture.

evidence.quote: The neural networks are implemented within the existing physics-based
Both networks N1 andN2 are shallow, as they have two hidden layers with 32 nodes in each.

methods.canonical_name: ePBL (Energetic Planetary Boundary Layer, original scheme)

evidence.quote: one using the ePBL scheme as a control run

datasets.canonical_name: GOTM k-epsilon single-column simulations (second moment closure)
datasets.spatial_resolution: 1 m vertical grid spacing, 800 m column

evidence.quote: The SMC data used to train the networks is generated using the single column model
The time step is set at 60 s, and the vertical grid spacing is 1 m. The depth of the column is 800 m.
Data was saved at hourly intervals.

datasets.canonical_name: JRA atmospheric forcing for GFDL OM4.0 ice-ocean model

evidence.quote: is forced using the JRA forcing product
The model has a nominal 1/4 degree resolution
The simulations were performed for a period of 1958 to 2017.

datasets.canonical_name: ARGO float measurements (mixed layer depth, stratification)

evidence.quote: ARGO float measurements have been utilized
data from the World Ocean Atlas (WOA)
Figure 9 shows the SST bias averaged over the years 2003-2017
